stories.headline: Heavy rain brings cheer to farmers but disrupts normal life in parts of north Telangana
stories.bodyText:
Moderate to heavy rains lashed several parts of north Telangana in the last 24 hours, bringing cheer to farmers amid El Nino concerns but disrupting normal life in parts of Mancherial and Jagtial districts on Wednesday.
Bellampalli mandal in Mancherial district was among the most affected with a tank breaching at Kannala village and inundating nearby agricultural fields, sources said.
Traffic was disrupted in the Ramnagar area of Bellampalli town after rainwater stagnated on a bridge. Several parked vehicles were damaged after trees were uprooted by strong winds. Power supply was also disrupted for some time, sources added.
In Jagtial district, rainwater surrounded a State-run school near a tank at Indira Priyadarshini Colony in Metpalli town.
Vehicular traffic on the Jagtial-Dharmapuri main road was disrupted as swollen streams overflowed while a portion of the road between Aksaipally and Nagaram villages was reportedly damaged.
Rainwater entered several houses in low-lying areas of Nerella and various other villages in the district, causing severe inconvenience to the villagers. The affected villagers were forced to wade through stagnant rainwater, while normal life in several other parts of the district was disrupted.
Jagtial recorded 18.9 cm rainfall in a span of 24 hours, ending 8 a.m. on Wednesday.
Published - July 29, 2026 09:12 pm IST

stories.headline: Youth killed as car crashes into electric pole in Kerala’s Kannur
stories.bodyText:
A 25-year-old man was killed and two others injured after the car in which they were travelling crashed into an electric pole and overturned at Kalaroad near Mattannur in Kannur in the early hours of Wednesday (July 29, 2026).
The deceased was identified as C. Sayanth of Kuthuparamba. He was driving the car at the time of the accident.
The injured, Abhiram 25, and Hrishiraj, 25, were admitted to a private hospital in Kannur. The accident occured around 1:15 a.m. The three were travelling from Irrity towards Kuthuparamba. The vehicle reportedly went out of control, hit an electric pole, and overturned.

stories.headline: Thrissur’s waste-to-wealth dream nears reality with 30-tonne biogas plant
stories.deck: Compressed biogas facility, expected to be commissioned by November 1, aims to tackle the city’s organic waste, generate green fuel and move Thrissur towards a zero-waste future
stories.bodyText:
Thrissur Corporation’s ambitious plan to end the city’s long-standing organic waste problem while producing clean energy is entering its final phase, with the construction of a compressed biogas (CBG) plant nearing completion near the Shaktan bus stand.
The facility, coming up on a two-acre site, will have the capacity to process 30 tonnes of biodegradable waste a day and convert it into compressed biogas, organic manure, and liquid fertilizer. The civic body is targeting its commissioning by November 1. Corporation officials said nearly 70% of the construction has been completed. The project is expected to cost around ₹12 crore.
According to the Corporation’s Health wing, the old municipal area alone generates between 25 tonnes and 30 tonnes of biodegradable waste every day from markets, hotels, apartment complexes and households. With waste from the areas merged into the Corporation also expected to be routed to the facility, the plant is likely to receive its full design capacity of 30 tonnes a day.
‘No pollution’
Mayor Niji Justin said the project would not cause environmental pollution and would be a major step towards sustainable urban waste management.
“The new plant will not cause any environmental pollution. We expect to commission it under the Chief Minister’s 100-day programme. A trial run is planned by the middle of September. Products from the plant will be marketed under the Corporation’s own brand. Our goal is to achieve zero waste,” the Mayor said.
The project received a major boost after the Corporation council recently approved emergency works worth ₹4.7 crore to complete the facility. These include a fertilizer packaging unit and a gas cylinder bottling unit, both considered essential for commercial operations.
The compressed biogas plant will scientifically process organic waste, purify the methane generated, and compress and store it under high pressure. The gas can be used as an alternative to CNG for vehicles.
According to Corporation sources, processing 30 tonnes of organic waste will yield around one tonne of compressed biogas every day. The plant is also expected to produce four to six tonnes of organic manure and about 12 kilolitres of liquid fertilizer daily.
New revenue stream
The biogas, manure and liquid fertilizer will be marketed, creating a new revenue stream for the civic body while reducing the cost of waste management. At present, a similar compressed biogas facility is functioning at Brahmapuram under the Kochi Corporation.
Once operational, the plant is expected to scientifically process biodegradable waste generated at the Shaktan and Jayhind markets as well as other major commercial centres in the city. Besides improving urban sanitation, the project is expected to remove rotten garbage from the streets and help curb the spread of vector-borne diseases.
The Corporation also sees the project as a key component of its broader vision to transform Thrissur into a green and sustainable city by reducing carbon emissions, promoting renewable energy and adopting a circular economy approach to waste management.
Published - July 29, 2026 09:09 pm IST

stories.headline: Perambra drug trafficking case: DIG reviews progress of probe
stories.deck: Police suspect the involvement of more persons in the drug deals and say the source of the drugs and money will be exposed in the forthcoming phase of the investigation
stories.bodyText:
Deputy Inspector General (North zone) K. Karthik, who reviewed the progress of the ongoing investigation into the Perambra drug trafficking case, on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) said that one of the five accused received over ₹1 crore from suspected drug buyers in the past six months alone.
He said the fifth accused, who was working as a delivery agent with a parcel company, had no other steady source of income to earn such a huge fund within a short time.
Explaining the progress of the probe under a special investigation team (SIT) formed by District Police Chief (Kozhikode Rural) Merin Joseph, he said similar illegal transactions were noticed in the accounts of all the other accused in the incident. “We suspect the involvement of more persons in these drug deals. The source of the drugs and money will be exposed in the forthcoming phase of investigation,” he added.
According to Mr. Karthik, the digital evidence gathered by the SIT could uncover the mutual relationships between the five arrested persons. The police have also moved court seeking the custody of the remanded individuals, including the three special instructors, to proceed with a detailed interrogation, he added.
Published - July 29, 2026 09:05 pm IST

stories.headline: Police probe alleged deposit-based packaging job scam in Devanahalli
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru police have detained a couple for allegedly cheating several people through dubious part-time job offers in northeast Bengaluru’s Devanahalli.
The accused have been identified as Kiran Kumar and Arathi. The police are tracking their bank accounts after around 15 people approached them alleging that they had been cheated of lakhs of rupees.
According to the police, there are a few more accused in the case whose roles are being ascertained. The group allegedly distributed pamphlet advertisements along with morning newspapers publicising the scheme.
According to the police, the accused presented the job as packaging work. Interested individuals could choose between a four-month or a 12-month scheme. After selecting a scheme, they could decide how many kilograms of packaging work they wished to undertake. For each packaging slab, individuals had to make a certain deposit in return for a monthly salary. At the end of the four-month or 12-month period, the total amount received would exceed the deposit made, which was projected as the profit.
For example, if a person opted to package 200 kg per month under the 12-month scheme, the individual had to deposit ₹ 1 lakh upfront. Every month, the individual was required to package 200 kg of items and would receive an approximate monthly salary of ₹ 23,000. At the end of the year, the individual would have earned nearly double the amount invested.
A senior police officer told The Hindu the accused would send the items and packaging materials to the individuals, who were asked to complete the work at their homes. The accused would subsequently collect the packaged items.
“We have questioned the accused, and they claim it is a legitimate packaging business and that they have been paying the stakeholders. We are ascertaining their claims,” the officer said.
The case came to light when one of the investors did not receive the promised salary for several months. Police have registered an FIR under Sections 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with cheating, and 316, which deals with criminal breach of trust. They have also invoked the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019.
Published - August 08, 2026 12:58 am IST

stories.headline: Scrap warehouse catches fire in RT Nagar
stories.bodyText:
A scrap warehouse in north Bengaluru’s R.T. Nagar went up in flames on Friday, with the fire spreading to adjoining properties, sources said.
The incident unfolded around 10.20 a.m. A source in the Fire and Emergency Services Department said a short circuit may have triggered a spark that led to the fire. However, the exact cause is yet to be ascertained. “Three fire tenders were dispatched, and it took over four hours to contain the blaze,” the officer said.
According to the officer, the situation was tense as a transformer was located close to the site of the fire, and several vehicles were also parked nearby. The incident once again exposed the hazards posed by garbage blackspots, as the fire spread to an adjacent site where a large garbage blackspot had formed.
Keerthika, a resident of the locality, told The Hindu that the blackspot had existed for a long time. “It is legacy waste that has been dumped there. Mounds of soil have also accumulated, and weeds have grown over them,” she said.
Published - August 08, 2026 12:56 am IST

stories.headline: 8 medals, 1 message: Two queer athletes from Bengaluru claim international glory in Spain
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Breaking societal barriers, two queer athletes from Bengaluru returned from Spain with eight medals between them after representing India at the recently concluded International Gay Games in Valencia.
Gowthami Kandhasami, 26, and Sumit Pawar, 35, competed in various athletic events at the games, organised by the Federation of Gay Games to celebrate sports and culture, with a focus on LGBTQIA+ identities and allies. Three resident Indians participated in the tournament.
Gowthami, who goes by the nickname Goaty, won four gold medals in the women’s 25-29 age category — in high jump, 5km run, 10km indoor run, and marathon. She also won silver medals in the 10km run, overall women’s marathon, and mixed 4x400m.
Gowthami Kandhasami, (Goaty) earned four Gold medals in High Jump, 5km Run, 10m Indoor Run and Marathon in the Women's 25–29 category and two Silver medals 10K Run in the Women's 25–29category, Overall Women's Marathon, and as part of the Mixed 4×400mRelay team.
“I always considered myself as a weak athlete physically since I was very young. I wasn’t the one who won a lot, but the one who always participated,” Goaty said at a felicitation event organised by All India Professionals’ Congress in Shantinagar here Thursday.
Born and brought up in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, Goaty moved to Bengaluru for her master’s degree. 
After relocating to the city during lockdown, she joined Bengaluru Frontrunners, a community for LGBTQIA+ runners and walkers.
“I’ve been running with Bengaluru Frontrunners since 2021, which changed how I felt inside my body. We all might be able to relate to how disconnected we feel with our bodies as queer people. So every time I finished a race or a run, the connection that I felt with the body was positive,” she said.
A Thalaghattapura resident, Goaty balanced her job as a school teacher with training. She said queer athletes face the same challenges as other athletes, while also dealing with additional barriers.
“Both of us got a scholarship from the organisers and the runners club in India to participate in the games. Otherwise, it would not have been possible. This time, only three Indian resident athletes were there. Next year, we want to improve the numbers,” she added.
Pawar, a Rajasthan native who works at Bengaluru’s Museum of Art and Photography (MAP), won gold in javelin throw. He said moving to Bengaluru three years ago gave him an opportunity to engage with the queer sporting community.
“In India, we never think about sports as a profession, and even those who make it a profession do so because of some kind of privilege. When I moved to Bengaluru three years ago, that was the first time I could start running around with the queer community,” he said.
Sumit Pawar,  brought further glory to India by winning the GoldMedal in the Javelin Throw. .
Pawar, a resident of Cambridge Layout in Ulsoor, said the sporting community’s focus on male and female categories often excludes those who identify as neither.
Representing the country was among the best moments of his life. “There was an opening ceremony and we entered the stadium with the Indian flag. That day, I was not from the queer community. I was an athlete representing India,” he said.
Sumit Pawar,  brought further glory to India by winning the GoldMedal in the Javelin Throw. .
The athletes said queer sportspersons continue to face discrimination in sports and society. Pawar cited former Indian sprinter 
Dutee Chand
, who faced backlash in her home village after coming out as lesbian. “We’re only asking for a proper space for us to train and perform. The state govt needs to explore options for athletes in categories outside the male and female binary. Even if people don’t want to talk to us, that’s fine, but they should provide us the opportunity to train and participate,” Pawar appealed.

stories.headline: Report faults Bidadi Township land acquisition, farmers demand rollback
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Farmers opposing the proposed Bidadi Township on Friday released a report by a panel headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice V Gopala Gowda that alleged the acquisition of nearly 9,600 acres in Bengaluru South district is illegal. Farmers urged the govt to withdraw the land acquisition notifications and scrap the project.
The report, titled ‘Judgement of Public Hearing’, was released by Samyukta Horata Karnataka and Joint Action Committee of Farmers. It said the preliminary and final notifications were issued without legal authority and are therefore void 
ab initio
.
Farmers argued that Greater Bengaluru Development Authority, constituted under the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, has no jurisdiction to acquire land under the Karnataka Urban Development Authorities (KUDA) Act. They argued that only the Ramanagara Urban Development Authority, established under the KUDA Act, is empowered to issue such notifications.
The report also alleged that the acquisition was initiated without preparing a mandatory statutory development plan. It said there was no approved master plan demarcating roads, water supply, electricity, parks, playgrounds or other civic infrastructure, making the process contrary to the KUDA Act.
It further claimed that mandatory provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, were ignored.
The report says the govt did not conduct a social impact assessment, public hearing, expert appraisal or independent evaluation of public purpose. It also questioned Rule 29-A of Karnataka Rules, alleging it replaces statutory rehabilitation and resettlement benefits with a one-time compensation of up to Rs 5 lakh.
The report also flagged environmental violations, stating that the proposed township falls under Category B1 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Notification, 2006, requiring prior environmental clearance. It alleged that no such clearance was obtained before the notifications were issued.
The report claims the acquisition includes around 9,600 acres of irrigated farmland with more than four lakh coconut trees, over 10 lakh trees, nearly 2,000 acres of mulberry cultivation and extensive vegetable farms. It said the region’s dairy sector supplies around 1.5 lakh litres of milk to Bengaluru every day.
It claimed most affected farmers opposed the project and that the few instances of consent cited by authorities were obtained under fear and confusion rather than through free and informed agreement.

stories.headline: Health department forms 30 special teams to inspect hotels, restaurants, food outlets across Bengaluru
stories.deck: According to the notification from Health and Family Welfare Department, the inspection will be conducted in five-star hotels, road-side eateries, restaurants and other forms of food businesses.
stories.bodyText:
Following complaints received from public, videos posted on social media platforms and media reports, the Health and Family Welfare Department has formed 30 special teams to conduct inspections in hotels, restaurants, smaller food units and others.
The teams comprise officials from Food Safety and Drug Administration.
U.T. Khader, Minister for Health and Family Welfare, said, “We were receiving continuous complaints from various people and through videos posted on social media about the sale of substandard food, unhygienic practices at eateries, etc. Every citizen has right to clean and healthy food. From Friday (August 7, 2026), we have started the inspection drive in five-star hotels in Bengaluru.”
He added, “These teams are being led by Food Safety Commissioner, Srinivas K. and they will inspect the food and hygiene as per the guidelines of the Food Safety and Drug Administration department. I have instructed officials to submit a detailed report at the end of the day about actions being taken and the kind of violations noticed in these hotels, including big and small.”
According to the notification from the department, the inspection will be conducted in five-star hotels, road-side eateries, restaurants and other forms of food businesses. The inspection checklist is prescribed by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) for each hotel/food establishment. Inspection officials will record video at required locations in each hotel/food establishment for further investigation purposes.
The notification also stated that legal action will be taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011, in case of violations.
It says that a review should be conducted on the caloric value of food items, and officials have to inspect if ingredients like milk or masala items have expired, if the kitchens are hygienic, if food is stored under prescribed temperature, if hotels are using banned colour to prepare gobi manchurian, curries and non-vegetarian items, while also reviewing cross-contamination prevention measures, and cold chain management.
Further, necessary steps should be taken to collect food samples of sheep, chicken, fish and other meat products and submit them to a private laboratory for analysis.
After conducting the inspection in each of the designated hotels, food establishments, the address of the centralised kitchen of the said food establishment should be obtained and a visit should also be made there for inspection.
The department has also requested citizens to raise complaints of food safety violations by dialling the FSSAI helpline number posted on its website.
On Friday, 26 three-star and five-star hotels in Bengaluru were inspected and a total of 35 food samples were collected and sent to the Food Laboratory for analysis.
Inspections revealed several food safety violations, including unhygienic food handling and storage conditions, fungal growth on vegetables, failure to maintain separate storage for vegetarian and non-vegetarian food items, noncompliance with FSSAI labelling requirements, improper labelling and others, stated a release.
Around 76 kg of meat and 200 kg of vegetables were seized from a five star hotel in the city. In addition, 32 litres of expired milk were seized and destroyed. In another hotel, three kgs of expired bakery products found were also seized. Around 105 kg of expired food articles, comprising chicken, meat, fish and vegetables were seized from a few more hotels in the city.
The release further stated that notices were served to the Food Business Operators (FBOs), and adjudication proceedings before the Adjudicating Officer under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 will be initiated.
Published - August 07, 2026 05:44 pm IST

stories.headline: ​Pay wall: On a charge on UPI transactions
stories.deck: Removing UPI’s free nature will not only be unpopular but also unfair
stories.bodyText:
The government’s decision to allow banks and payment processors to levy a charge on UPI transactions, while still pending, has already led to several policy questions. No official decision has yet been announced, but the preparations are apparent. The only official change that has been made is the amendment to the Payment and Settlements Systems Act that will now allow the government to notify which types of transactions can attract a charge. This was done through the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which was passed in the Lok Sabha recently without a debate. Before this law, UPI and RuPay debit card transactions were expressly exempt from any charges. Government sources say that the charge could be allowed only for transactions conducted by large merchants with turnovers of more than ₹1 crore-₹1.5 crore and for transactions above ₹2,000 in value. This would limit the charge to only about 5% of all UPI transactions. However, the amended law gives the government the ability to widen this scope. The fear also is that merchants will pass this cost on to consumers, who will move back to cash, which remains free to use. That said, the issue must also be looked at from the point of view of the payment ecosystem. UPI was made free in 2020. The payments players have argued that they have been bearing the cost of maintaining and running UPI since then. As Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra recently said, “somebody has to pay” for UPI. Presumably, he meant that “somebody” should no longer be the payment processors or banks.
However, the burden of the cost has not solely been borne by these players. Taxpayers are already bearing some of it. In 2021, the government introduced a scheme where it paid these payment processors and banks a subsidy to partially cover the cost of processing transactions up to ₹2,000 done by small merchants. The government has already paid about ₹11,349 crore on this, with another ₹2,000 crore budgeted for 2026-27. The question is whether consumers and merchants should be asked to pay an additional charge when some of their taxes are already being used for this purpose. There is also some anger over the perception that the government pushed people towards UPI through demonetisation, only to now allow it to become chargeable. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has argued that such a charge will help payment players invest more on infrastructure, innovation, and security. The RBI has the resources to pay for UPI’s development. Using this would entail a small reduction in the vast surplus that it transfers to the Centre each year, but it would save the government from an increasingly unpopular decision.
Published - August 08, 2026 12:20 am IST

stories.headline: Prudent approach: On the RBI’s interest rate-setting committee meeting
stories.deck: The RBI did well to hold interest rates, but inflationary pressures remain
stories.bodyText:
There was little room for the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)’s interest rate-setting committee to manoeuvre during its meeting in early August. Elevated global crude prices over the past few months had already pushed retail inflation beyond the central bank’s 4% target, with headline CPI rising to 4.38% in June, the highest in the current CPI series. While the outcome was a foregone conclusion, leading the RBI to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% for the fourth consecutive meeting, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra’s post-MPC statement suggests that the central bank’s principal concern has, for some time now, been containing the fallout of mounting geopolitical uncertainties on India’s macroeconomic fundamentals. The recent dollar-rupee swap and the decision to absorb the hedging cost on fresh Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposits are clear indications of the RBI’s focus. The objective is twofold: to maintain adequate domestic liquidity as the rupee weakens amid capital outflows, while shoring up foreign exchange reserves as the merchandise import bill swells on the back of elevated crude prices. Foreign exchange reserves have now climbed close to $700 billion, while FCNR(B) deposits have risen to around $40 billion and are expected to grow further before the scheme closes. The rupee, which until recently was the worst-performing Asian currency, has recovered to around ₹95.
However, the MPC’s assessment that inflationary pressures are not yet broad-based and remain largely confined to food and fuel may prove premature. Higher fuel costs have affected sectors including transport, food, travel, and tourism. Inflation in transport services more than doubled to 4.31% in June from 1.75% in May. Although the Centre cut commercial LPG prices for a second consecutive month in July, it is unrealistic to expect restaurants and eateries to pass on these savings immediately. Passenger vehicle manufacturers have also raised prices this year, reflecting higher input and logistics costs. While U.S. President Donald Trump has indicated a possible truce and a durable arrangement to secure navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, the Ukraine war continues to threaten supplies from Russia, India’s largest crude supplier. Even so, the RBI’s decision to prioritise growth while remaining alert to inflationary pressures from global supply shocks is underpinned by India’s relatively strong domestic fundamentals. Merchandise exports grew 15.5% year-on-year in June, consumption demand has remained resilient, and public and private investments continue to strengthen. Governor Malhotra’s assertion that future policy decisions will remain “data dependent” and that the RBI will adopt a “wait-and-watch” approach is arguably the most prudent course.
Published - August 08, 2026 12:10 am IST

stories.headline: SEBI did not penalise most finfluencers: CFA study
stories.deck: CFA survey asks investors to verify credentials, understand the education versus advice distinction, use regulated investment platform and be cautious of terminology.
stories.bodyText:
Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) did not penalise 95.8% of influencers even though many of their activities showed warning signs or raised concerns, according to CFA Institute’s survey.
In a survey of 48 influencers and their behaviours in 2025, released in 2026, the CFA found SEBI’s action or involvement was found only in 6.25% of the fininfluencers.
Identifying several key issues surrounding how finfluencers offer investment advice and disclose their collaborations; it said some finfluencers do not explicitly mention paid collaborations. It is difficult for viewers to find out whether content has been paid for and by whom.
Some do not explicitly identify the brands involved in paid partnerships; instead, they refer to products or services in generic terms, which can obscure the commercial nature of the content, said the authors in the report titled “Clicks and Credibility 2.0: From Influence to Accountability, Disclosures, and Policy Impact.”
Finding that conflicts of interest are common; the survey said finfluencers might have their own business in related areas, such as wealth advisory, taxation, or providing legal help for start-ups and businesses. Such business activities may get a boost from the finfluencer activity by creating an impression of expertise. Potential and current clients/customers for those related businesses may be influenced as a result.
The sample showed that 62.5% disclosed their conflicts of interest, such as sponsored content or affiliate marketing. The remaining 37.5% did not. However, this does not necessarily indicate an undisclosed conflict, as some may not have had any commercial arrangements to disclose during the period reviewed.
Some finfluencers also organize offline sessions, often with followers, in which they suggest stocks and give advice, it said, adding some offer stock suggestions indirectly. “This observation has been based on anecdotal evidence around finfluencer activity and not specifically related to the sample set in this study,” it said.
Although the share of SEBI registered finfluencers increased modestly, it remains firmly in the minority, it said. Moreover, the proportion of finfluencers providing stock recommendations remains unchanged at approximately one-third, indicating that the underlying gap between regulated activity and current practice persists, according to the survey.
Highlighting the “wide gap” between how many finfluencers are SEBI-registered and how many offer explicit stock recommendations; it said in the total sample, only three 6.3% are SEBI-registered; the remaining 45 (93.7%) are not registered,
Of the 16 finfluencers in the sample whose content the survey identifies as explicit stock recommendations, only two of these are SEBI-registered; implying that 14 of those finfluencers are making explicit investment recommendations that may warrant further examination from the regulator.
Regulations had worked well on some grounds. More than 72% of the surveyed influencers mentioned investment norms and nearly 67% of them were not giving recommendations.
Finding that the investing landscape is undergoing a structural shift, marked by the rapid rise of finfluencers who are increasingly shaping how retail investors perceive and evaluate investment decisions; it recommended investors to verify credentials, understand the education versus advice distinction, use regulated investment platform and be cautious of terminology.
Published - July 28, 2026 10:38 pm IST

stories.headline: Alembic Pharma gets U.S. FDA nod for generic chronic constipation drug
stories.bodyText:
Generic drugmaker Alembic Pharmaceuticals has received final approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its abbreviated new drug application for Prucalopride Tablets, 1 mg and 2 mg, used to treat chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC).
The approved ANDA is therapeutically equivalent to Takeda Pharmaceuticals USA Inc.’s reference-listed drug, Motegrity Tablets (1 mg and 2 mg), the company said on Tuesday.
Prucalopride Tablets had an estimated U.S. market size of $100 million for the 12 months ended March 2026, Alembic said citing IQVIA data. A serotonin-4 receptor agonist drug, it is indicated for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) in adults.
Published - July 28, 2026 10:34 pm IST

stories.headline: City Union Bank Q1 net rises 25% to ₹383 crore
stories.bodyText:
City Union Bank (CUB) reported a 25% year on year (YoY) increase in net profit to ₹383 crore for the first quarter. During the same period last year, the bank’s net profit was ₹306 crore. The bank’s Interest income rose 24% YoY to ₹ 1,985 crore during the quarter, while interest expenses increased by 19% to ₹1,165 crore.
As a result, net interest income (NII) grew 31% to ₹820 crore. Last year during the same period NII stood at ₹625 crore. Other income remained flat at ₹244 crore. CUB’s advances grew 25% YoY to ₹67,645 crore, while deposits increased 21% to ₹79,342 crore. As of June 30, 2026, the bank’s total business stood at ₹1.47 lakh crore, up 23% from a year ago. The retail, agriculture and MSME (RAM) portfolio, including non-agriculture gold loans, accounted for 80% of the bank’s total advances.
Published - July 28, 2026 09:55 pm IST

stories.headline: TNPL | We have a team that can qualify for playoffs: Kovai Kings captain Shahrukh
stories.bodyText:
Shahrukh Khan, captain of two-time TNPL champion Kovai Kings, expressed confidence in delivering a good show in the 10th edition.
The Kovai franchise finished sixth last year, failing to advance to the playoffs for the first time since 2021. But the skipper believed that the team, playing under a new ownership and rebranded as Vida Kovai Kings, had all the ingredients to put up a much better performance.
“I always try to pick a young team, and we’ve done that this year as well. There’s a new face to the franchise with new owners. We all feel that we have a team which can qualify. After that, it is just one game at a time,” said Shahrukh at the jersey unveiling event on Tuesday.
A settled core of players helped Kings win the title in 2022 (shared with Chepauk Super Gillies) and 2023 and led them to a runner-up finish in 2024.
Having lost some of his key members at last year’s auction, Shahrukh said that the side was focused on rebuilding its nucleus. The core is set to include R.S. Ambrish, who was part of the India under-19 World Cup-winning squad earlier in the year.
“Yeah, it’s good to have people from u-19s come and play. They’ve seen the pressure. They’ve played finals in u-19s. Obviously, this pressure is a bit more than what it is there. But still, these guys respond well to any situation that’s given to them,” Shahrukh remarked.
Published - July 29, 2026 07:19 pm IST

stories.headline: The ‘best is yet to come’ for Ayush Badoni
stories.deck: The 26-year-old, who will be leading South Delhi Superstarz in the third edition of the Delhi Premier League, says India-A exposure helped him gain confidence
stories.bodyText:
Ayush Badoni has had five seasons with Lucknow Super Giants in the Indian Premier League. Over the past 12 months, he has also featured regularly for India-A across formats. The opportunities are a reflection of his potential as a hard-hitting middle-order batter and a part-time off-spinner, but it hasn’t yet translated into match-defining performances.
The 26-year-old from Delhi admits he was subpar in the most recent IPL. Despite getting to bat higher up the order, his returns were a meagre 215 runs in 10 matches at an average of 21.5. It was followed by three outings for India-A in a 50-over tri-series involving Sri Lanka-A and Afghanistan-A in June, where his scores read 24, 0 and 15.
“Definitely, I feel I can perform better. The best is yet to come,” Badoni, who will lead South Delhi Superstarz in the third edition of the Delhi Premier League from Friday, told reporters at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Wednesday.
Badoni’s floundering form during IPL 2026 was compounded by LSG’s wooden-spoon finish. “It is challenging to be consistent as a player when the team is losing matches. The motivation goes down. Next year, we will hope to make amends,” he said.
Badoni remains determined to turn things around, for he knows that the national selectors are taking note of his contributions. “Playing for India-A gives you exposure and boosts your confidence. The selectors have told me to focus on my consistency as much as possible and to keep working on my bowling,” informed Badoni.
Published - July 29, 2026 06:08 pm IST

stories.headline: Gill skips Day 1 of practice game against SLC XI due to finger injury
stories.deck: Gill picked up the niggle during a training session here on Thursday (August 5) and as result, K.L. Rahul is leading the side in his absence
stories.bodyText:
India captain Shubman Gill will not take the field on the opening day of the practice match against SLC XI here on Friday (August 7, 2026) after sustaining an injury to his right finger during practice.
Gill picked up the niggle during a training session here on Thursday (August 5) and as result, K.L. Rahul is leading the side in his absence.
SLC XI has won the toss and opted to bat in the three-day practice game.
"Captain Shubman Gill sustained an impact injury to his right ring finger during India's practice on Thursday. As a precautionary measure, he will not take the field on Day 1 of the warm-up game against SLC XI. The BCCI Medical Team is monitoring his progress," the BCCI posted on its 'X' handle.
"KL Rahul will lead the team in Gill's absence."
India are touring Sri Lanka for a two-Test series, starting at Galle on August 15.
The second Test will be played here from August 23.
Published - August 08, 2026 04:30 am IST
